concerns.concern: The chemical potential is fixed to zero at the charge neutrality point at every temperature. Any real temperature dependence of μ(CNP) adds an error to the entropy that grows linearly with filling, and this could be the dominant systematic error.
concerns.quote: μ is obtained by integrating dμ/dn from the CNP and fixing μ(CNP) = 0 at every temperature.

concerns.concern: The extracted entropy decreases with rising temperature at ν = 2 and ν = 3, which violates thermodynamic stability. This points to systematic errors as large as the claimed plateau features.
concerns.quote: dS/dT < 0 violates thermodynamic stability (C > 0). This indicates systematic errors of the same size as the claimed plateau features.

concerns.concern: Fig. 4b shows negative entropies at 5 K with error bars of about ±1 k_B. This is unphysical and indicates large systematics.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4b shows negative entropies at 5 K, with error bars of order ±1 k_B. This is unphysical

concerns.concern: Main-text Eq. 3 silently drops the ρ(E_F) term that appears in Methods Eq. 7. This assumes ρ(E_F) ≪ ρ(E_F+eV_b), which is questionable in a partially filled flat band where the DOS at E_F is largest.
concerns.quote: Eq. 3 therefore implicitly assumes ρ(E_F) ≪ ρ(E_F+eV_b). This must be stated explicitly.

concerns.concern: ρ(E_F) lies inside the phonon gap, so the approximation cannot be checked from the data. The resulting filling-dependent error could create or suppress the dip–peak structure.
concerns.quote: The resulting error is filling-dependent and could generate or suppress the dip–peak structure.

concerns.concern: The analysis assumes a rigid spectrum whose DOS does not depend on filling, but MATBG reconstructs strongly with filling. The neglected ∂ρ/∂n terms would contaminate dμ/dn exactly where the cascade occurs.
concerns.quote: The neglected ∂ρ/∂n terms enter dI/dV_g directly and would contaminate dμ/dn precisely where the cascade occurs.

concerns.concern: An elastic tunneling model is applied even though the tunneling is phonon-assisted (inelastic). The phonon energy shift, matrix element and occupation are absent from Eqs. 1–7.
concerns.quote: Eq. 1 is an elastic tunneling model, but the authors state that tunneling is phonon-assisted (inelastic).

concerns.concern: The exponential transmission background T(n) is empirical. The proposed barrier-height mechanism should give only a tiny effect, and the fit and its fitting range are not shown.
concerns.quote: The form T(n) ∝ exp(0.258 n/n₀) is empirical.

concerns.concern: Errors in the fitted background exponent propagate into dμ/dn but are not quantified. In particular, it is unclear whether the negative dμ/dn values survive plausible variations of T(n).
concerns.quote: are the negative dμ/dn values robust against plausible variations of T(n)?

concerns.concern: dμ/dn is shown only at V_b = ±42 mV. Extractions at several biases are needed to show that this thermodynamic quantity is bias-independent.
concerns.quote: Extractions at several biases, for example ±30, ±42, ±55 mV, are needed to demonstrate robustness.

concerns.concern: The effective mass is simply proportional to the inverse of dμ/dn. The heavy-to-light transitions are therefore a re-plotting of the dμ/dn structure, not independent evidence.
concerns.quote: The manuscript should not present them as an independent observation.

concerns.concern: The quoted heavy masses come from regions where dμ/dn approaches zero or turns negative. There small offsets dominate and the formula diverges, and the negative regions are silently omitted from the plots.
concerns.quote: Negative regions are silently omitted from the plots.

concerns.concern: The calculated entropy curves rise monotonically above ~15 K and do not show the second plateau claimed in the caption. The theoretical ν = 0 curve also does not match the data at 20 K.
concerns.quote: the caption's claim that "below and above 15 K the entropy shows two plateaus" is therefore not supported by the plotted curves.

concerns.concern: The entropy plateaus rest on a few sparse temperature points from a 3-point derivative, with error bars comparable to the differences being interpreted. The shaded plateau regions appear to be chosen by eye.
concerns.quote: The error bars are comparable to the differences being interpreted.

concerns.concern: The measured entropy values do not quantitatively match the local-moment counting model at ν = 3, ν = 0 and ν = 2. A table of predicted versus measured values with uncertainties is needed.
concerns.quote: Provide a table of predicted versus measured values with uncertainties.

concerns.concern: Treating f-electrons as decoupled local moments at 10–20 K is not obviously justified, given f–c hybridization of ~20–25 meV and inter-site exchange of order meV.
concerns.quote: Treating f-electrons as decoupled local moments at 10–20 K (1–2 meV) is not obviously justified.

concerns.concern: The boundary condition S(ν = 4) = 0 is contradicted by the authors' own model at 20–30 K. It is also imposed where the filling correction is largest, so the sensitivity of S to it should be shown.
concerns.quote: Show the sensitivity of S to this boundary condition.

concerns.concern: The entropy values (~4 k_B per moiré cell at 20 K) are several times larger than those reported in prior SET work at comparable fillings and temperatures. This discrepancy is not discussed.
concerns.quote: This discrepancy must be discussed, not omitted.

concerns.concern: A 10 meV gap was measured at the CNP, yet the entropy at ν = 0 rises from ~0 to ~4 k_B between 12 and 20 K. These need to be reconciled.
concerns.quote: Yet the entropy at ν = 0 rises from ~0 to ~4 k_B between 12 and 20 K.

concerns.concern: The itinerant c-electron and phonon entropy contributions are not separated from the local-moment entropy. A T-linear background alone would prevent a true plateau.
concerns.quote: A T-linear background alone would prevent a true plateau.

concerns.concern: The heavy-below/light-above asymmetry requires locating integer fillings to much better than 0.1. No filling uncertainty is given for each integer.
concerns.quote: A filling uncertainty for each integer should be given.

concerns.concern: Only one device is reported. Reproducibility of the ν = 2 gap, the mass asymmetry and especially the entropy plateaus across devices and cooldowns is not shown.
concerns.quote: Only one device is reported.

concerns.concern: In resistive insulating states, part of the bias and AC excitation may drop across the sample or contacts rather than the junction. This could produce artificial dark lines and dμ/dn peaks, so contact and sheet resistances versus filling should be reported.
concerns.quote: A fraction of V_b (and of the AC excitation) could then drop across the sample/contacts rather than the junction

concerns.concern: Tunneling from graphite via a specific phonon is momentum-selective rather than a probe of the momentum-integrated DOS. Orbital-selective matrix elements could bias the very f/c asymmetry being claimed.
concerns.quote: Orbital-selective matrix elements could therefore bias exactly the f/c asymmetry being claimed.

concerns.concern: The statement E_F = μ(n) ~ ±22 mV conflates the Fermi energy, the filling-dependent chemical potential and the filling-independent phonon threshold. This confusion propagates into Eq. 2 and the Methods derivation.
concerns.quote: The statement "E_F = μ(n) ~ ±22 mV" mixes three distinct quantities.

concerns.concern: None of the dμ/dn curves carries uncertainties, although the mass and entropy analyses depend on small values and on differences between them.
concerns.quote: None of the dμ/dn curves (Figs. 2a, 3a, 4a) carries uncertainties

concerns.concern: A fixed degeneracy g′ = 4 is assumed even though the cascade changes flavor degeneracy. A change from 4 to 1–2 alters m* by a factor of 2–4 and could mimic part of the asymmetry.
concerns.quote: A degeneracy change from 4 to 1–2 across an integer filling changes the inferred m* by a factor of 2–4

concerns.concern: No discriminating test separates the mass interpretation from symmetric/symmetry-broken phases or reset/Dirac-revival explanations. A Lifshitz–Kosevich analysis or direct cyclotron-mass measurement is suggested.
concerns.quote: No discriminating test is offered.

concerns.concern: The main text attributes the 4→8 crossover to isospin local moments, while Ext. Fig. 3b attributes it to heterostrain-split flat bands with charge transfer. A strain-split multiplet would also give a smooth Schottky-like crossover rather than two flat plateaus.
concerns.quote: A strain-split multiplet produces a smooth Schottky-like crossover, not two flat plateaus.

concerns.concern: It is not shown that a strain of ε = 0.001 in the THF model produces the ~1–2 meV splitting needed for a crossover at ~15 K.
concerns.quote: Show explicitly that ε = 0.001 in the THF model produces this splitting.

concerns.concern: U₁ and ε are tuned to match the data. The number of tuned parameters versus features reproduced, a sensitivity analysis, and an independent heterostrain estimate are needed.
concerns.quote: U₁ = 23 meV and ε = 0.001 are "set to match the experimental data".

concerns.concern: Each so-called plateau spans only a factor of ~1.5 in temperature. This is insufficient to establish temperature-independent local-moment behavior.
concerns.quote: Each plateau spans only a factor of ~1.5 in temperature (8–12 K, 16–26 K).

concerns.concern: The abrupt entropy jump between 4.2 K and ~6 K implies an enormous heat-capacity peak and may be an endpoint-derivative artifact. The ground-state region is defined by only one or two points.
concerns.quote: it is unclear whether it is physical or an artifact of the endpoint derivative.

concerns.concern: Temperature-dependent changes of the tunneling channel and background may not have been accounted for, for example by re-fitting T(n) at each temperature. Any such artifact feeds directly into ∂μ/∂T and hence the entropy.
concerns.quote: Was T(n) re-fitted at each temperature?

concerns.concern: It is not described how the sample temperature was measured and stabilized up to ~40–77 K in a ³He system. Whether junction properties drift with temperature is also not addressed.
concerns.quote: Describe how the sample temperature was measured and stabilized up to ~40–77 K in a ³He system.

concerns.concern: Local moments emerging at finite fields are claimed, but no field-dependent entropy, ∂μ/∂B, or in-plane-field tests are shown.
concerns.quote: These are the standard tests for local moments (cf. Saito et al.) and should be added, or the claim removed.

concerns.concern: The claim that local moments have eluded experimental confirmation overlooks prior entropic and heavy/light-asymmetry reports. The new contribution relative to that work needs to be stated precisely.
concerns.quote: The introduction says local moments have "thus far eluded experimental confirmation".

concerns.concern: The dμ/dn magnitudes, negative-compressibility depths and total chemical-potential swing are not quantitatively compared with published SET data.
concerns.quote: should be compared with published SET data (Zondiner, Rozen, Saito).

concerns.concern: The 26 meV integrated bandwidth is not reconciled with the 16 mV band separation seen spectroscopically in Fig. 1b.
concerns.quote: The 26 meV integrated bandwidth should also be reconciled with the 16 mV band separation seen spectroscopically in Fig. 1b.

concerns.concern: The electron and hole halves of dμ/dn appear to be measured at opposite biases, i.e. under different electrostatic conditions. How they are stitched, and whether this affects electron–hole asymmetry claims, is unexplained.
concerns.quote: Explain how they are stitched and whether this affects electron–hole asymmetry claims.

concerns.concern: The 42 mV bias induces about 0.5 n₀ of doping and a displacement field of opposite sign on the two sides. Its effect on the flat bands and the cascade is not discussed.
concerns.quote: Its effect on the flat bands and on the cascade should be discussed.

concerns.concern: Capacitive pickup from the AC gate modulation, and any phase offsets, could contaminate dI/dV_g. How these were removed is not described.
concerns.quote: Describe how this pickup and any phase offsets were removed from dI/dV_g.

concerns.concern: dI/dV_b and dI/dV_g are measured separately, so drift or gate hysteresis enters Eq. 3 directly. The claimed 'ultra-stable' junction is not demonstrated.
concerns.quote: Quantify the junction stability, since "ultra-stable" is asserted but not demonstrated.

concerns.concern: The large quantum-capacitance filling correction is deferred to the SI. It should be done self-consistently over the full filling range, including C_b.
concerns.quote: It should be done self-consistently over the whole filling range, including C_b.

concerns.concern: The claim that the quantum-capacitance correction is negligible away from band edges is doubtful near ν = 0 and ν = 2, where gaps also exist.
concerns.quote: The claim that the correction is "negligible away from band edges" is doubtful near ν = 0 and ν = 2

concerns.concern: Graphite is a semimetal with low, energy-dependent DOS, so assuming a constant probe DOS is unjustified. The bias shifts its Fermi level, and its quantum capacitance should modify C_b.
concerns.quote: Constant probe DOS is unjustified.

concerns.concern: Summing over a range of phonon momenta implies several meV of broadening, which undercuts the claimed high energy resolution. An estimate should be provided.
concerns.quote: This implies a broadening of several meV, which undercuts the claimed "high energy resolution".

concerns.concern: The assignment to a 20 meV ZA phonon needs justification, since in-plane phonons at that momentum lie at 50–70 meV. The material, the exclusion of other branches, and the 22 mV versus 20 meV discrepancy must be explained.
concerns.quote: the 20 meV ZA assignment needs explicit justification.

concerns.concern: It is unclear how AFM determines the lattice orientation. If it is inferred from flake edges, a 12° misalignment is possible, which would imply a different momentum mismatch and a different phonon.
concerns.quote: the zigzag/armchair ambiguity allows 12° as well as 18°.

concerns.concern: The quantity from Eq. 4 includes Hartree and exchange-correlation contributions. Calling it a cyclotron effective mass is therefore misleading.
concerns.quote: Calling it a "cyclotron effective mass" is misleading.

concerns.concern: The m* ≈ 0.01 m_e near ν = 4 reflects the band-gap dμ/dn peak rather than a quasiparticle mass. Gap regions should be excluded from mass plots.
concerns.quote: Gap regions should be excluded from mass plots.

concerns.concern: The light mass (~0.06 m_e) is lighter than the LL-derived flat-band mass and comparable to the remote-band mass. It should be checked against the THF c-electron velocity rather than compared with bilayer graphene.
concerns.quote: This should be checked quantitatively against the THF c-electron velocity, rather than compared with bilayer graphene.

concerns.concern: Mass swings at negative fillings, where THF predicts a mirrored asymmetry, are visible but not analyzed. They would be a valuable consistency test.
concerns.quote: These are not analyzed, although they would be a valuable consistency test.

concerns.concern: In Fig. 3c the theory at 20 K is compared with data at 0.3 K and 4 K. The theory also shows ν = 2 structure at 20 K although the experimental gap vanishes by 4 K.
concerns.quote: The theory is computed at T = 20 K but compared with data at 0.3 K and 4 K.

concerns.concern: In Fig. 3c the theory and data use different units, and 'good agreement' is asserted without any quantitative comparison.
concerns.quote: "Good agreement" is asserted without any quantitative comparison.

concerns.concern: The IKS state is a low-temperature ordered phase, so its relevance to a 20 K calculation needs explanation.
concerns.quote: its relevance to a 20 K calculation needs explanation.

concerns.concern: A 1.3 meV gap should survive at 4 K, yet the sharp ν = 2 peak appears only at 0.3 K and the caption says the gap opens below 4 K. This inconsistency is unexplained.
concerns.quote: A 1.3 meV gap (≈15 K) should not be washed out at 4 K

concerns.concern: Estimating the ν = 2 gap from the μ change over ν = 1.9–2.1 includes ordinary band dispersion and so overestimates the gap. The background slope should be subtracted.
concerns.quote: it overestimates the gap. The background slope should be subtracted.

concerns.concern: A g-factor of 5.4 with g ≠ 2 implies orbital or valley contributions. The conclusion of a spin-unpolarized intervalley-coherent singlet therefore does not follow uniquely.
concerns.quote: The conclusion of a "spin-unpolarized ... intervalley coherent spin singlet" therefore does not follow uniquely.

concerns.concern: The constant ν = 2 gap below 1.5 T is unexplained.
concerns.quote: The constant gap below 1.5 T is unexplained.

concerns.concern: The extrapolated zero-field gap of 1.75 meV is inconsistent with the measured 1.3 meV.
concerns.quote: The extrapolated Δ₀ = 1.75 meV is also inconsistent with the measured 1.3 meV zero-field gap.

concerns.concern: Landau quantization of the graphite probe up to 8 T could modulate the probe DOS and produce features in the field-dependent maps. A control or discussion is required.
concerns.quote: The graphite probe develops its own LLs up to 8 T.

concerns.concern: In the LL mass fits, V_b is treated as energy although it also dopes the sample, by up to ~1.7 n₀ for the remote bands. The lever arm and doping must be included before quoting masses.
concerns.quote: The lever arm and doping must be included before quoting m* = 0.047 and 0.174 m_e.

concerns.concern: The Chern-number assignments lack the Streda fits, slopes and uncertainties, and the restrictive s·ν > 0 convention is not justified.
concerns.quote: Show the Streda fits, slopes and uncertainties. Justify the restrictive convention s·ν > 0.

concerns.concern: Hole-side entropy is not presented, although the counting model makes explicit predictions for ν < 0.
concerns.quote: Hole-side entropy is not presented

concerns.concern: The Pomeranchuk-like effect in Fig. 4e is not discussed in the text. The plotted fillings are not ν = 1, and the HFL/LM shading is unjustified.
concerns.quote: The "Pomeranchuk-like effect" is not discussed in the text.

concerns.concern: The abstract implies strain is verified experimentally, but no strain is measured; it enters only as a fitting parameter.
concerns.quote: no strain is measured. Strain enters only as a fitting parameter.

concerns.concern: Negative compressibility signals dominant exchange/correlation energy. It does not by itself indicate a more stable lower-energy state.
concerns.quote: It does not by itself indicate "the emergence of a more stable lower energy state".

concerns.concern: The analogy to Mott-insulator compressibility is inappropriate for a peak displaced from integer filling.
concerns.quote: The analogy to Mott-insulator compressibility (Ref. 44) is not appropriate

concerns.concern: STM shows LDOS concentrated at AA sites. Claiming f-electrons were directly observed by STM/STS overstates those works.
concerns.quote: Stating that f-electrons are "experimentally observed via STM/STS" overstates what those works show.

concerns.concern: Twist-angle and strain homogeneity within the ~1 µm² probe area is not characterized. Inhomogeneity would broaden features and affect entropy at integer fillings.
concerns.quote: Twist-angle and strain homogeneity within the ~1 µm² probe area is not characterized

concerns.concern: Essential analysis steps are deferred to the SI, and data are only available on request, so the analysis cannot be evaluated or reproduced. A public data and code deposit is recommended.
concerns.quote: the analysis cannot currently be evaluated or reproduced. A public data and code deposit is recommended.

concerns.concern: Whether the TBG is aligned to either hBN, the usual cause of a sizeable CNP gap, is not stated, nor how alignment was checked.
concerns.quote: Is the TBG aligned to either hBN? State how alignment was checked

concerns.concern: The temperature to which the mass renormalization persists is quoted inconsistently as ~50 K, ~70 K and ~77 K. Fig. 3b, cited for the 50 K claim, shows only 0.3 K and 4 K.
concerns.quote: The text says the renormalization persists to "~50 K" citing Fig. 3b, but Fig. 3b shows only 0.3 K and 4 K.

concerns.concern: The field above which LL degeneracy is lifted is given as 3.5 T in the main text and 1.5 T in Methods.
concerns.quote: Methods states that all 0th-LL degeneracies are lifted above 1.5 T.

concerns.concern: The phrase 'a factor of 10 is determined in the m* renormalization' and the notation 'n/n₀ + δ' in the Fig. 3 captions are unclear or undefined.
concerns.quote: "A factor of 10 is determined in the m* renormalization" (Fig. 3d caption) is unclear.

concerns.concern: The entropy counting formulas are printed incorrectly and should be written as binomial coefficients.
concerns.quote: They are presumably binomial coefficients and must be written as such.

concerns.concern: The dashed interpolations between integer fillings in Fig. 4b have no physical meaning and should not be compared with non-integer data.
concerns.quote: The dashed interpolations between integer fillings in Fig. 4b have no physical meaning

concerns.concern: The claim that CNP entropy saturates to zero below 12 K, 'as also observed in SET', lacks a citation.
concerns.quote: has no citation, and it is unclear which SET result is meant.

concerns.concern: The twist angle is quoted inconsistently as 1.06°, 1.07° and 1.08° in different places.
concerns.quote: 1.06° ± 0.02° (main text), 1.08° (Fig. 1b caption) and 1.07° (Methods).

concerns.concern: The formula used to obtain the twist angle from n₀ is dimensionally incorrect.
concerns.quote: The formula θ = a(2/(√3 n₀))^{1/2} is dimensionally incorrect

concerns.concern: The gate calibration implies a gate capacitance of ≈0.048 µF/cm², inconsistent with the ≈0.10 µF/cm² expected for 30 nm hBN.
concerns.quote: n = 0.30×10¹² V_g cm⁻² implies C_g ≈ 0.048 µF/cm².

concerns.concern: Methods give thickness ranges rather than the actual hBN layer thicknesses of this device.
concerns.quote: The Methods give thickness ranges (2–6 layers, 30–50 nm) rather than the actual values for this device.

concerns.concern: The quoted band-edge gate voltage (~8 V) is inconsistent with the stated calibration, which gives ≈8.9 V for 4n₀.
concerns.quote: With the stated calibration, 4n₀ corresponds to ≈8.9 V.

concerns.concern: The LL formula differs between Methods, √(N(N+1)), and Ext. Fig. 2e, √(N(N−1)).
concerns.quote: Methods text uses √(N(N+1))B, while Ext. Fig. 2e uses √(N(N−1))B.

concerns.concern: 'Massive Dirac fermion' is used for what is actually the chiral bilayer-like LL spectrum.
concerns.quote: "Massive Dirac fermion" is used for what is the chiral (bilayer-like) LL spectrum.

concerns.concern: The LL indexing implies E₁ = E₀, which needs clarification.
concerns.quote: The indexing implies E₁ = E₀, which needs clarification.

concerns.concern: The Ext. Fig. 2a caption says 'high compressibility' for gaps between LLs, which should be low compressibility.
concerns.quote: "High compressibility of gaps between LLs" should read low compressibility (high dμ/dn).

concerns.concern: The Ext. Fig. 2c caption does not specify whether ν refers to moiré filling or Landau filling.
concerns.quote: "Fixed ν~1 near the CNP" does not say whether ν is the moiré filling or the Landau filling.

concerns.concern: Equation numbering in Methods is inconsistent: wrong equations are referenced and the numbering jumps from (7) to (11).
concerns.quote: "by solving equations (4) and (5)" should refer to (1) and (5), and numbering jumps from (7) to (11).

concerns.concern: The prefactors and the notation (ρ versus ρ_s) differ between main-text Eq. 2 and Methods Eq. 1.
concerns.quote: The prefactors and notation (ρ versus ρ_s) also differ between Eq. 2 and Methods Eq. 1.

concerns.concern: Several references are duplicated.
concerns.quote: Refs. 1 and 30 are the same paper, as are Refs. 28 and 60, and Refs. 23 and 57.

concerns.concern: A Kondo-lattice theory paper and an x-ray phonon dispersion paper are cited to support the tunneling-model assumptions, which is inappropriate.
concerns.quote: Refs. 27 (a Kondo-lattice theory paper) and 37 (x-ray phonon dispersion) are cited for the tunneling-model assumptions.

concerns.concern: Ref. 4 has garbled author names.
concerns.quote: Ref. 4 has garbled author names ("M. Haule, E.Y.A., K. Haule").

concerns.concern: The Ext. Fig. 1c caption refers to the wrong panel.
concerns.quote: Ext. Fig. 1c says "data in a" but should say b.

concerns.concern: The Fig. 2a caption ('below 4 K') conflicts with the main text.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 2a caption ("below 4 K") conflicts with the text.

concerns.concern: Fig. 3d uses a truncated log axis that hides the heavy mass values.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3d has a truncated log axis that hides the heavy values.

concerns.concern: There are several typos and a LaTeX residue in the text and references.
concerns.quote: "Wanatabe" → Watanabe (author list); "Seeback" → Seebeck; "valance" → valence; "filings" → fillings
